recordedBy: Michael J. Moore|Hilda Flores Olvera|Helga Ochoterena Booth|Norm Douglas
habitat: Growing on limestone hills. This area In small area of gypsum hills (ca. 2 km by 2 km) at foot of limestone hills. This area is actively mined for gypsum. Diverse gypsum endemic assemblage dominated by Agave, Fouquieria, Tiquilia mexicana, Haploesthes greggii, Nerisyrenia, Hedyotis, with numerous other taxa present including Nama cf. stenophyllum, Dicranocarpus, Acleisanthes purpusiana and Drymaria. Conditions reasonable to good.
locality: A gypsum outcrop ca. 10-15 km by gravel road  W of MEX 53.
occurrenceRemarks: Collected for the project “Origin and Evolution of the Chihuahuan Desert Gypsum Endemic Flora”.
name: Drymaria pattersonii B.L.Turner
